name: Question 10
problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14069185/assets/5243b22ebef45709f214ac2422cfb72528f24fd5ef51bd38aa3fc0ff40f1888d.png)

Consider the phase portrait for a decoupled system above.
Which of the following systems could correspond to the given portrait?
worked_solution:
Writing a decoupled system in matrix form, we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{\lambda }_{1} & 0 \\ 0 & {\lambda }_{2}\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

where $x(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}].$

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are parallel to the axes. These correspond to so-called straight-line solutions of the form

$$
{c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\,\text{and}\,{c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, notice that:

- The tangents along the $x$-axis are pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]$
must approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{1}>0.$

- The tangents along the $y$-axis are also pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form 
${c}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$
must also approach infinity as $t\to \infty .$ So, we must have ${\lambda }_{2}>0.$

Among the options, the only system that satisfies ${\lambda }_{1}>0$ and ${\lambda }_{2}>0$ is the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=4x(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=3y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

Consider the phase portrait for a decoupled system above. Which of the following systems could correspond to the given portrait?

a
{x′(t)=4x(t)y′(t)=3y(t)
b
{x′(t)=−4x(t)y′(t)=3y(t)
c
{x′(t)=−3x(t)y′(t)=−4y(t)
d
{x′(t)=−4x(t)y′(t)=−3y(t)
e
{x′(t)=4x(t)y′(t)=−3y(t)
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Writing a decoupled system in matrix form, we have x′(t)=[λ100λ2]x(t) where x(t)=[x(t)y(t)].

Since our system is decoupled, its eigenvectors are parallel to the axes. These correspond to so-called straight-line solutions of the form c1eλ1t[10]andc2eλ2t[01].

Now, notice that:

  • The tangents along the x-axis are pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form c1eλ1t[10] must approach infinity as t→∞. So, we must have λ1>0.

  • The tangents along the y-axis are also pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form c2eλ2t[01] must also approach infinity as t→∞. So, we must have λ2>0.

Among the options, the only system that satisfies λ1>0 and λ2>0 is the following: {x′(t)=4x(t)y′(t)=3y(t)
